title: Christian Beliefs: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the core Christian beliefs about God: Trinity, creation, incarnation and the nature of God.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Christian Beliefs foundations — Trinity, creation, incarnation, omnipotent God.
final_note: You now know the foundational Christian beliefs about God.

concepts.def: One God in three persons: Father, Son, Holy Spirit
God the Son becoming human in Jesus Christ
All-powerful — a key attribute of God
All-knowing — a key attribute of God
All-loving — a key attribute of God
God who made the universe from nothing (ex nihilo)

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christians believe in one God who is omnipotent (all-powerful), omniscient (all-knowing) and omnibenevolent (all-loving).

God is also just and merciful. These attributes shape how Christians pray, worship and live.

'God is love' (1 John 4:8) is a key verse.

Christians believe in one God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

At Jesus' baptism (Matthew 3:16-17) all three are present: the Son in the water, the Spirit as a dove, the Father's voice from heaven.

The Nicene Creed (325 CE) settled this teaching for the Church.

Genesis 1:1: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.' Christians believe God created the universe out of nothing (ex nihilo).

John 1:14: 'The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us.' The incarnation is God the Son becoming human in Jesus.
